n.story:
Your role remains deeply rooted in the physical world, but your 'eyes and ears' have been vastly extended by technology. While the core of your work—handling animals, assisting births, and maintaining hygiene—remains a manual and intuitive craft, AI has removed the guesswork from your administrative and monitoring duties. You no longer spend hours manually recording health metrics or calculating feed rations; sensors and automated systems now track every animal's movement, temperature, and growth in real-time, alerting you only when a specific animal needs your physical intervention.

This shift allows you to move from reactive care to proactive management. With AI-powered predictive analytics, you can identify signs of illness days before they become visible to the naked eye and optimize breeding cycles with scientific precision. You are less of a manual laborer and more of a biological data manager, using high-tech insights to ensure the highest standards of animal welfare and productivity. Your expertise is now amplified by a digital nervous system that monitors the farm 24/7.
